owned_invariants: The task is items, a nonempty list of weighted digraphs, and arms, a list of at least two objects each with its own text channel. An arm may hold checker_pin and budget. A task that is not of this form is refused before anything is asked.

arms_share_fixed_checker is recorded first: every arm's checker_pin is the pin of the grader as it is now. arms_share_budget is recorded second: every arm's budget has the same canonical form, a missing budget being null. If either fails the run ends there, refused as ARMS_NOT_MATCHED, with nothing asked.

Otherwise each arm in turn is asked each item, in order, under the stage channel:position. The prompt is the default prompt for the item with the arm's channel added, so it carries no statement and no reply of another arm.
A reply stands when its text, graded by the one grader on the item, is HOST_CERTIFIED or TYPED_REFUSAL. A missing reply, a reply that is not an object and a reply with no text do not stand.
accept_set_depends_only_on_bytes holds when no reply claims an accepted other than the boolean the grader gave it. The replies that do are listed as channel:position.

All held, the comparison is certified as CHANNELS_COMPARED with the number of replies that stood for each channel, and the discordant items of the first two arms: those the first arm's reply stood for and the second's did not, and the other way round.
boundaries: A comparison says which replies were certificates for these items under one grader. It does not say which channel is better in general.
Only the first two arms are paired; every arm is counted alone.
The host does not see how an arm made its reply, so a claim about the channel is the arm's word.

score.level_basis: Typed refusals on every failure path, closed requests, exact unbounded integers and rationals, no float, no unwrap or expect.

basis.G1: Module header declares AuthorityEffect None and the contract URN; public items match this contract and code/rust/pfp_operads/README.md. Not B: no requirement-to-symbol trace beyond the README and docs/plans/operads_redesign.md.
basis.G2: Exact: counts are exact integers, a budget is compared by its canonical form, and every grade is the exact grader's. Not B: tested on examples, not proven.
basis.G3: Each unreadable part of a task has its own reason, mismatched arms and a claim the grader does not give are their own refusals, and a missing reply is refused naming the stage. No panicking unwrap or expect, and no index. Not B: panic-freedom is tested, not proven.
basis.G4: 23 WF35 tests assert the registry entry, channels compared on one checker with each predicate and its evidence, arms that used another checker or another budget refused before anything is asked, a budget compared by its canonical form and every arm held to it, a channel that claims an acceptance the grader does not give and only the boolean it gave being honest, every claim listed with its channel and item, a parallel edge violation a mask accepts, a reply with no text or no reply at all, a reply that stands as a cycle or a potential, the discordant pairs for the first two arms and counts for the rest, missing and extra replies, each part of a task, channels that differ only in case, and no prompt that carries a reply or a claim. One mutant is recorded as demonstrably equivalent with its justification in the report. Mutation campaign R = 100/100. clippy -D warnings and rustfmt pass. Not B: mutants are hand-written one-line edits, not a generated campaign, and there are no generator-driven property tests.
basis.G5: Measured worst cyclomatic 10, cognitive complexity is not measured for Rust, nesting 2; ceiling A+, recorded A.

clippy with -D warnings on both crates, all targets.
